---
title: Manage tool context
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/manage-tool-context
description: Choose between tool search, programmatic tool calling, prompt caching, and context editing to manage context bloat.
---

Tool definitions and accumulated `tool_result` blocks consume your context window. Long-running agents with many tools or many turns can exhaust available context before the task is finished. Four approaches address this at different points in the pipeline.

## The four approaches

Each approach targets a different source of context pressure. Pick the one that matches where your tokens are going.

| Approach                  | What it reduces                         | When it fits                                                         | Learn more                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tool search               | Tool definitions loaded upfront         | Large toolsets (20+ tools) where most tools aren't needed every turn | [Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool)                         |
| Programmatic tool calling | `tool_result` roundtrips                | Chains of tool calls that can execute as a single script             | [Programmatic tool calling](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling)       |
| Prompt caching            | Token cost of repeated tool definitions | Stable toolsets across many requests                                 | [Tool use with prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching) |
| Context editing           | Old `tool_result` blocks in history     | Long conversations where early results are no longer relevant        | [Context editing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing)                                   |

### Tool search

Tool search keeps tool definitions out of the context window until Claude asks for them. Instead of sending 50 tool schemas upfront, you send a single `tool_search` tool and let Claude discover the rest on demand. This trades a small amount of latency (one extra turn to look up a tool) for a large reduction in baseline context usage.

### Programmatic tool calling

Programmatic tool calling collapses a sequence of tool calls into a single code block that Claude writes and Anthropic's code execution sandbox runs. Rather than five roundtrips of `tool_use` and `tool_result`, Claude emits one script that calls all five functions from within the sandbox. The intermediate results never enter the conversation history.

### Prompt caching

Prompt caching doesn't reduce the number of tokens in context, but it reduces what you pay for them on subsequent requests. If your tool definitions are stable, cache them once and reuse the cached prefix across thousands of requests. This is the right choice when the toolset is large but fixed.

### Context editing

Context editing removes old `tool_result` blocks from the conversation history once they've served their purpose. A long agent loop might produce hundreds of intermediate results that were useful at the time but are now dead weight. Context editing lets you trim them without restarting the conversation.

## Combining approaches

These approaches compose. A long-running agent might use tool search to keep the toolset lean, prompt caching to amortize the cost of the remaining definitions, and context editing to trim stale results as the conversation grows. Each solves a different part of the problem, so there's no conflict in using them together.

A reasonable starting point for a high-volume agent:

1. Enable prompt caching on your tool definitions from day one. Cache writes carry a 25% markup over base input pricing, which pays back on the second request that hits the cache.
2. Add tool search once your toolset grows past roughly 20 tools or your baseline context usage becomes noticeable.
3. Add context editing once individual conversations start running long enough that early results become irrelevant.
4. Consider programmatic tool calling if you notice repetitive chains of small tool calls that could run as a single batch.

## Next steps

    Collapse tool-call chains into a single executable script.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Tool use with prompt caching" icon="database" href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching">
    Cache tool definitions across requests to cut token costs.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Context editing" icon="scissors" href="https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing">
    Trim stale tool results from long-running conversations.

</CardGroup>

I found relevant information about the OpenAI Responses API and the `store: false` behavior with function calls.

## Key Findings:

**Function Call ID Matching with `store: false`:**

The `call_id` alone pairs the call with its `function_call_output`, so the function call and its output are correlated by this identifier. This is important when replaying function calls.

**The Core Issue:**

When replaying tool calls, the function_call.id refers to an item the server stored, but when `store: false` is set, that id names nothing. This can cause problems because a relay that synthesizes its own item ids (a UUID rather than fc_...) therefore poisoned a topic permanently: the bad id was written into the persisted history and every later turn replayed it.

**The Fix:**

The solution is to drop the id from replayed function_call items (upstream fix in 3.0.73), since `call_id` alone pairs the call with its `function_call_output`.

**Validation Requirements:**

Empty or whitespace-only function_call.call_id is rejected by the Responses decoder, and empty or whitespace-only function_call_output.call_id is rejected instead of producing an empty tool correlation ID.

results:
I found relevant information about the OpenAI Responses API and the `store: false` behavior with function calls.

## Key Findings:

**Function Call ID Matching with `store: false`:**

The `call_id` alone pairs the call with its `function_call_output`, so the function call and its output are correlated by this identifier. This is important when replaying function calls.

**The Core Issue:**

When replaying tool calls, the function_call.id refers to an item the server stored, but when `store: false` is set, that id names nothing. This can cause problems because a relay that synthesizes its own item ids (a UUID rather than fc_...) therefore poisoned a topic permanently: the bad id was written into the persisted history and every later turn replayed it.

**The Fix:**

The solution is to drop the id from replayed function_call items (upstream fix in 3.0.73), since `call_id` alone pairs the call with its `function_call_output`.

**Validation Requirements:**

Empty or whitespace-only function_call.call_id is rejected by the Responses decoder, and empty or whitespace-only function_call_output.call_id is rejected instead of producing an empty tool correlation ID.

The "No tool output found" error typically occurs when there's a mismatch between the `call_id` in a replayed function_call and the corresponding function_call_output, particularly when using `store: false`.

content.text:
The other agent's answers hold up. I checked every code claim against this worktree and the two API vendors' docs. Everything it stated as fact is accurate, and the things it labeled as guesses are correctly labeled as guesses. Two points need correcting or adding.

**What checks out**

- Between turns the app rebuilds history from the saved chat as role plus text only, capped at the last 20 messages. That is exactly [AgentHost.cpp:1648](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1648) through 1669.
- Within one turn the provider keeps the full input, including tool results. The comment is at [OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:204](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:204).
- The printer chat turns the workspace off and notes on at [PrinterConversation.cpp:261](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:261). The "notes in context" flag is a real per-session switch the same change could copy.
- The provider's call id is not saved. The saved activity record keeps the tool name, arguments, result, state, and the assistant message it belongs to, but no call id. The host holds the call id only while the turn is live, at [AgentHost.cpp:1757](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:1757).
- A rejected card is reported back as cancelled, at [PrinterConversation.cpp:361](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:361).
- The prompt test copies the text-only history on purpose. Its own docstring says so. Note that this test exists only on the other branch, at commit 52be072920, not in this worktree.
- Best practice is as the agent described. Anthropic's docs say to keep a running message list and append to it, and treat clearing old tool results as a threshold-based trimming strategy, not the default. OpenAI's guide appends the whole previous output, calls included, to the next input.

**What to correct or add**

1. There is a trap the agent did not mention. Each function call the model returns carries two ids: a `call_id` that links it to its result, and an item `id` that names a server-stored object. With storage off, that item id refers to nothing, and other projects have hit errors by replaying it. So when replaying saved calls, send the call id and omit the item id. Whether a client-made call id is accepted is not documented anywhere I found. Saving the real one is a one-field change, so I would do that rather than test the undocumented case.
2. The printer chat is less blind than the answer implies. The system prompt already lists the printers on the network with their serials, at [printerInstructions.ts:78](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:78). The app's notes about a verified, added, or cancelled connection already reach the model. And the connect tool accepts the printer's name in place of its id and lists the valid ids when it refuses, at [PrinterConversation.cpp:292](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:292). Replaying tool history still fixes the root cause, but the current failure is narrower than "the information is lost".
3. One small detail: after each tool call the app starts a new assistant message, so a turn with two tool calls is three assistant messages, and all of them count toward the 20-message cap.

**The "why does the app drop them" answer** is honestly marked as a guess, and the code supports only part of it. The comment explains why notes are skipped in the project chat. Nothing in the code states why tool calls and results are dropped, so that remains inference.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06

---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: agent-setup-api-key-path
description: "JusPrin Agent setup, API-key route — verification-is-construction design, privacy rule for the probe, and the routes deliberately left unbuilt."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: eb922e6b-d324-4167-adb6-c08ea83efb8f
  modified: 2026-09-14T16:29:41.120Z

Commit `d4012fe1df` on `jusprin-newui` (2026-09-01) built the API-key route of
Agent setup, the destination of the previously inert "Set up the agent" button
from `454e9a1b5f`. Design comes from the Figma file **JusPrin v2**, page
"Agent Setup - Empty State" (5 frames). See [[agent-bridge-phase-5]] for the
preceding phase.

**Verification and construction are the same act.** `ProviderKeySetup` checks a
key by running one real request through the same `OpenAIResponsesAgent` the
Agent will use, and hands that already-connected instance back as the outcome.
A key that passes cannot drift apart from an Agent that works, and the
"replied in 0.8 s" shown is the measurement that happened. Prefer this over a
separate validation call if this is ever extended to another provider.

**The probe carries no project data.** It sends a fixed sentence and an empty
workspace snapshot: a provider the user has not chosen yet must not receive
their workspace just to prove a key works. A test asserts this.

Structure: setup is poll-driven like `IAgentService` so `AgentHost` stays
deterministic; the probe is GUI-free and unit-testable; the commit step
(AppConfig only; the key is `jusprin_agent.openai_api_key` since 2026-09-14, moved out of the Keychain because every unsigned rebuild re-prompted) is injected from `AgentConfiguration.cpp`, which is also
where completing the flow records `cloud_consent`. Threaded through as
`AgentRuntime::setup`. Protocol grew `setup_check_key` / `setup_cancel` /
`setup_status` under an `agent_setup` capability, no version bump — see
[[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]].

**Deliberately not built, in priority order:** an Anthropic adapter (so the
design's default tab is disabled and the screen opens on OpenAI); the "Other…"
provider (meaning undefined); "Continue with JusPrin" (no account backend
exists in the repo — needs the auth endpoint, flow shape, and whether the app
receives a JusPrin token or a provider key); "Run a model on this machine"

---
name: printer-prompt-card-wording-breaks-connect
description: "Bambu connect fails ~30% because the app drops tool results between turns, so the model invents deviceIds; tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py measures prompt changes in seconds without the app"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f665746c-cfdb-4776-8406-cafeefecc864
  modified: 2026-09-24T04:14:16.760Z
---

Found 2026-09-24 on branch claude/printer-receipt-card, by recording the app's OpenAI requests through a local proxy (`JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`).

**The root cause.** Between turns, AgentHost sends only the messages' text. It sends no function calls and no function_call_outputs. In turn 1 the model calls printer_connection_status and learns `deviceId: FAKE001`, then says "I found one A1 mini". On "Yes, connect it" that result is gone, so a model that calls printer_connect without checking again invents an id (`<from_status>`, `A1 mini`, `<deviceId from printer_connection_status>`) and gets unknown_device. Unfixed when this memory was written. Candidate fixes: put the discovered candidates in the connect session's context, or keep a session's tool results across turns.

**Rates**, from `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (connect-bambu):
- Shipped prompt: about 64% (32 of 50).
- With a prompt line about the "Printer added" receipt card: 4 of 20.

The app-based runs agreed in direction. That line stays out.

**Why small prompt edits swing it (ablation, 2026-09-24, 60 to 90 runs per variant):**
- The model almost never looks the printer up again on "connect it" (0-15% of runs).
- A run passes only when its first reply happens to quote the display name "JusPrin Fake A1 mini", which the app accepts as an id: those runs pass about 87% of the time. The rest of the time the model rebuilds an id from the name, e.g. JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI.
- When the reply doesn't name the printer and the model doesn't look again, the run fails every time (0 of 129).
- Quoting the name is incidental style that any edit shifts: the shipped prompt names it in 83% of runs, neutral unrelated sentences in about 60%, the receipt line in 38%, and the full receipt change in 19%.
- Pinning the drop on particular words ("do not repeat its name") was inconclusive.

**The lightweight test:** run_prompt_tests.py uses only Python's stdlib plus node. It renders the prompt from printerInstructions.ts via render_prompt.mjs, sends printer_tools.json (guarded by a test in test_openai_responses_agent.cpp; regenerate with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1), and copies the text-only history. 20 runs take about 20 s. The shell harness's --printer-connect-trials mode was built, then removed in favour of it.

**Why:** single app runs are single samples. 0/3 vs 3/3 was once over-read as "the shipped prompt works".

**How to apply:** judge printer prompt edits with run_prompt_tests.py, 20 or more runs per side. Add new cases there, not to the shell harness. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

**Addendum 2026-09-23 (branch claude/printer-connect-async):** the runner was
still only on claude/printer-receipt-card; copied into a scratchpad and given
cases for host failure wording, "skip", the wait length, and the full list.
Lesson: an edit to the *connect* rules ("enter the connection details
themselves in the printer settings") dropped the unrelated "show me the full
printer list" step from 94% (85/90) to 73% (66/90), and only when the Add
session's context carried the real 383-printer catalogue plus a network
printer; a 3-printer toy session showed no drop. Dropping "themselves" fixed it
(29/30). Measure unrelated cases with the real session payload (dump
panel->session_json() from the harness) whenever the prompt changes.

On "Yes, connect it" that result is gone, so a model that calls printer_connect without checking again invents an id (`<from_status>`, `A1 mini`, `<deviceId from printer_connection_status>`) and gets unknown_device. Unfixed when this memory was written. Candidate fixes: put the discovered candidates in the connect session's context, or keep a session's tool results across turns.

**Rates**, from `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (connect-bambu):
- Shipped prompt: about 64% (32 of 50).
- With a prompt line about the "Printer added" receipt card: 4 of 20.

The app-based runs agreed in direction. That line stays out.

**Why small prompt edits swing it (ablation, 2026-09-24, 60 to 90 runs per variant):**
- The model almost never looks the printer up again on "connect it" (0-15% of runs).
- A run passes only when its first reply happens to quote the display name "JusPrin Fake A1 mini", which the app accepts as an id: those runs pass about 87% of the time. The rest of the time the model rebuilds an id from the name, e.g. JUSPRIN_FAKE_A1_MINI.
- When the reply doesn't name the printer and the model doesn't look again, the run fails every time (0 of 129).
- Quoting the name is incidental style that any edit shifts: the shipped prompt names it in 83% of runs, neutral unrelated sentences in about 60%, the receipt line in 38%, and the full receipt change in 19%.
- Pinning the drop on particular words ("do not repeat its name") was inconclusive.

**The lightweight test:** run_prompt_tests.py uses only Python's stdlib plus node. It renders the prompt from printerInstructions.ts via render_prompt.mjs, sends printer_tools.json (guarded by a test in test_openai_responses_agent.cpp; regenerate with JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PRINTER_TOOLS=1), and copies the text-only history. 20 runs take about 20 s. The shell harness's --printer-connect-trials mode was built, then removed in favour of it.

**Why:** single app runs are single samples. 0/3 vs 3/3 was once over-read as "the shipped prompt works".

**How to apply:** judge printer prompt edits with run_prompt_tests.py, 20 or more runs per side. Add new cases there, not to the shell harness. See [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

**Addendum 2026-09-23 (branch claude/printer-connect-async):** the runner was
still only on claude/printer-receipt-card; copied into a scratchpad and given
cases for host failure wording, "skip", the wait length, and the full list.
Lesson: an edit to the *connect* rules ("enter the connection details
themselves in the printer settings") dropped the unrelated "show me the full
printer list" step from 94% (85/90) to 73% (66/90), and only when the Add
session's context carried the real 383-printer catalogue plus a network
printer; a 3-printer toy session showed no drop. Dropping "themselves" fixed it
(29/30). Measure unrelated cases with the real session payload (dump
panel->session_json() from the harness) whenever the prompt changes.

content.text:
Done. The printer chat now sends the model its earlier tool calls and their results on every turn, the project chat is unchanged, and a live check against the real model shows the "made-up printer id" failure gone. Nothing is committed.

**What changed**

- A new per-session switch, tool history in context, sits beside the existing notes switch in [AgentService.hpp:52](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentService.hpp:52). The printer chat turns it on. The project chat leaves it off, so its requests are byte-for-byte what they were.
- The provider's call id is now saved with each tool activity, as a `callId` field in the project document. Old records without it are simply not replayed. The id is handed in at proposal time through one extra argument on the coordinator's propose call.
- When the switch is on, the host inserts each earlier call right after the assistant message that made it, as one history entry holding both the call and its result. A pair can never be split by the 20-entry cap, so no call is ever sent without an answer. The result text is built by the same helper the live path uses, so the model sees exactly what it saw when the call ran.
- The OpenAI adapter emits those entries as a function call followed by its output, using the saved call id and omitting the server's item id. With storage off that item id names nothing, and other projects have hit errors by replaying it.

**Verification**

- Three new tests: the printer session replays the call with the live result and the project session does not, the wire format has exactly the expected fields, and the call id survives a save and reload. With the printer switch turned off, the first test fails, so it guards the behaviour. The full suite passes:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| agent_bridge_tests | 254 cases, 5000 assertions, all passed |

- Live check against the shipped model, using the printer session's real tools and rendered system prompt. The person says "is it online?", the app looks the printer up, then the person says "Yes, connect it":

| History sent | Correct connect call | What went wrong otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text only, as before | 0 of 5 | Two sent a Moonraker host type for a Bambu printer, one used the name as the id, two looked again |
| With the replayed call | 5 of 5 | none |

That also confirms the service accepts the replayed shape.

**Left out**

- The prompt test script on the printer receipt card branch, at commit 52be072920, still copies text-only history. It is not on this branch, so it needs the same change when the branches meet. The live-check recipe is saved in memory so it can be repeated in about thirty seconds.

content.text:
Honest answer: I added the switch mostly for caution, not because I found a case where replay is wrong.

**Why I added it**

- It kept the project chat's requests byte-for-byte unchanged, so the only behaviour I changed was the one I could measure. I measured the printer chat live and got 5 of 5. I did not measure the project chat at all.
- It mirrors the existing notes switch, which already treats the two chats differently for a stated reason.
- The other agent's plan proposed a per-session switch and I followed it without questioning it hard enough.

**The reasons I wrote in the comment, checked honestly**

- "A stale result would contradict the workspace snapshot." This is weaker than it sounds. My replay helper already leaves the workspace part out of each result, so a replayed project-chat result is just the tool's own outcome. And the assistant's own text already restates those outcomes, such as "I sliced it, two hours", so the model sees stale facts today anyway. The prompt's rule to use only ids from the current workspace context guards the part that matters.
- Size. Project tool results can be large, such as a settings search or a slice report, and the cap counts entries, not bytes. This is a real cost concern but a cap on bytes would solve it without a switch.
- Unmeasured risk. The main chat drives real project changes through approval cards, and I have no evidence either way for how the model behaves with its own earlier calls in view.

**Scenarios where off is genuinely right**

I could not find one. The general practice, which I confirmed earlier from both vendors' docs, is to keep the whole transcript and trim selectively when it grows. A chat that deliberately hides its own tool history from the model is the unusual case, and the printer chat was the proof of what that costs.

**Recommendation**

Remove the switch and replay everywhere, with two guards: a byte cap on each replayed result, and a project-chat measurement before it ships, using the same live-check method as the printer chat. The test I wrote that asserts the project chat replays nothing would flip to assert that it does. If you would rather ship the printer fix first and widen it separately, the switch is the seam for that, but it should not stay as a permanent design.
